label: Pancam Mast Assembly (PMA)
function: Twin multispectral stereo Panoramic Cameras (Pancam) with 8-position filter wheels for geological mineralogy mapping, plus wide-angle monochrome Navigation Cameras (Navcam) for autonomous path planning and hazard detection.
missionFacts: Captured over 217,000 raw images during 5,352 Martian sols of operation
Pancam images revealed hematite-rich 'blueberries' at Eagle Crater confirming ancient standing water
Navcam enabled autonomous navigation — Opportunity could drive several meters per command cycle
Last Pancam color panorama captured from Perseverance Valley in April 2018 before the global dust storm

label: Rocker-Bogie Mobility System

specs.wheel_diameter: 26 cm aluminum wheels with 19 machined cleats

function: Springless articulated six-wheel mobility system. Two rocker arms joined by an internal differential crossbar passively distribute weight across all wheels on uneven terrain without any active suspension control.
missionFacts: Successfully escaped the 'Purgatory Dune' sand trap on Sol 446 after 37 days of carefully planned extraction
Climbed and descended the 32-degree inner slope of Victoria Crater during 1-year crater rim investigation
Total traverse of 45.16 km — the longest distance driven on another planet at the time of mission end
Wheels left visible tracks in Martian regolith observed in HiRISE imagery from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

label: Triple-Junction GaAs Solar Arrays

specs.peak_power: ~140 W at beginning of mission (Mars solar constant)
specs.degradation: ~0.14% per sol dust accumulation (between cleaning events)

function: Gallium arsenide multi-junction photovoltaic panels converting sunlight to electricity. Charged two 8-Ah lithium-ion batteries providing power during night survival and peak demand operations.
missionFacts: Designed for 90-sol life before expected fatal dust accumulation — far exceeded by 14+ years
Martian dust devil cleaning events repeatedly restored panel output to near-beginning-of-mission levels
Power dropped from 900 watt-hours to <45 watt-hours per sol as global dust storm peaked in June 2018
Final power failure occurred ~15:00 PDT June 10, 2018 when storm blocked ~99% of incoming sunlight

label: Instrument Deployment Device (IDD)

specs.degrees_of_freedom: 5 (shoulder azimuth, shoulder elevation, elbow, wrist azimuth, wrist elevation)
specs.turret_instruments: MI + APXS + Mössbauer Spectrometer + Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT)

function: Five degree-of-freedom robotic arm deploying a science turret carrying four in-situ contact instruments. Precisely placed instruments against rock and soil targets chosen by scientists on Earth.
missionFacts: Ground into over 100 rock targets using the RAT diamond-bit grinding tool during the 14-year mission
APXS analysis of Eagle Crater outcrop rocks confirmed sulfate minerals formed in standing liquid water
Mössbauer Spectrometer identified hematite and jarosite — minerals requiring acidic aqueous environments
IDD was last commanded on Sol 5109; arm position at mission end is consistent with its final survey pose

label: High-Gain Steerable Dish Antenna (HGA)

specs.pointing: 2-axis gimbal, tracks Earth position across Martian sky

function: Gimbaled parabolic dish antenna providing direct X-band communication to NASA Deep Space Network stations on Earth, independent of orbiter relay infrastructure.
missionFacts: Transmitted directly to DSN stations at Goldstone (California), Canberra (Australia), and Madrid (Spain)
Used for primary science data downlink each afternoon sol following peak solar power period
Signal travel time to Earth ranged from 3.0 to 21.0 minutes depending on Mars-Earth orbital geometry
Supplemented by UHF relay through Mars Odyssey and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter for higher data rates
